# proxy-protocol-runtime

Repository-authored, sanitized NGINX migration fixture for issue #366 (imported HTTP PROXY-protocol identity evidence, per #366's 2026-09-21 amendment). It uses only synthetic local addresses, hostnames, paths, and values; it contains no production configuration, credentials, or external endpoints.

The exact assessment contract, candidate disposition, categories, origin, and license are recorded in `manifest.json`. It reuses the `#426` `listen ... proxy_protocol;` + `real_ip_header proxy_protocol;` + `set_real_ip_from` translation and proves the resulting `[[servers]] proxy_protocol = "in"` / `[servers.client_address] trusted_proxies` runtime security boundary end to end through a real Jul instance: a real local relay bound to the one trusted source address prepends a genuine PROXY v1 header asserting an arbitrary client address, which Jul honors as the canonical client (observable in the `X-Forwarded-For` it forwards upstream); the same bytes sent from an untrusted direct peer are refused outright rather than served on a spoofed or fallback identity, per the documented "a connection from an address outside the set is refused" contract (`docs/configuration.md`).

The real-Jul E2E lives in `cmd/jul/corpus_runtime_test.go` (`TestNGINXCorpusProxyProtocolRealE2E`) rather than the generic manifest `scenarios` array, because it needs to control the raw TCP peer address and inject a raw PROXY protocol header before the HTTP request, which the generic single-request/response Scenario/Dimension model does not express. Every dial in the test originates from the ordinary default loopback address (127.0.0.1) — the only loopback address guaranteed present without extra host configuration on every CI platform, since macOS does not auto-alias 127.0.0.0/8 to lo0 the way Linux does. The trusted and untrusted positions are produced instead by running two Jul instances with different `trusted_proxies` values against that same peer address: one running the fixture's own unmodified translated candidate (`trusted_proxies = ["127.0.0.2/32"]`, straight from `set_real_ip_from`) to prove the untrusted/CIDR-mismatch refusal, and a second with `trusted_proxies` overridden to `["127.0.0.1/32"]` purely so the peer check can be satisfied on every platform, used for the trusted-peer positive cases. It also asserts three further cases: the trusted relay asserting identity with a **PROXY v2 binary header** (built with `internal/proxyproto.WriteV2`, the same encoder Jul's own outbound `proxy_protocol = "out"` path uses) is honored exactly like the v1 text form, since Jul's listener parses both wire versions through the same shared `internal/proxyproto.ReadHeader`; a malformed PROXY header from an otherwise-trusted peer is refused (trust in the source address does not extend to trusting arbitrary bytes); and a client-supplied `X-Forwarded-For` cannot override the PROXY-derived canonical identity.

This E2E is H1 only and loopback-only; no pinned real-NGINX reference lane runs this fixture today (`scripts/nginx-migration-e2e.sh` is HTTP-only, and PROXY protocol is a TCP-preamble mechanism with no HTTP/3-over-QUIC equivalent). H2/H3 client-identity parity for the underlying runtime capability is already #259's obligation, not a migration-specific claim.
